Steps to reproduce: Sign up, then verify the token the app just issued, with the app clock set to a time that differs from the machine clock.
What was wrong and the fix applied: The JWT verifier checked expiry against the system clock while tokens were issued with the app clock, so a fresh token was refused as 'used before issued'. Verifier now takes the app clock (`AuthService`). Also made token expiry testable.
The server answered 500 and logged a stack trace. `Api.body()` now catches every parse and type error and raises InvalidInputException, so the answer is 400.

Steps to reproduce: GET / and read the response headers.
What was wrong and the fix applied: The home page and static files had no Content-Security-Policy, nosniff or frame headers. Javalin does not run after-handlers for static files, so the headers set there never applied. The same header map is now given to the static file config.

Steps to reproduce: Boost a listing, open the home page, look at the first card.
What was wrong and the fix applied: The Featured badge sat on top of the save heart in the top-right of the card. Moved to the bottom-left of the photo (`style.css`).

The template pinned PostgreSQL engine version 16, which cfn-lint reports as no longer allowed for new RDS instances. The engine version is now a parameter and `deploy.sh` asks AWS for the current default version. Confirmed on 2026-11-25: RDS created the instance with the looked-up version in ap-southeast-2.
YAML parse error: a colon inside an unquoted description. Description quoted. Same run also flagged an unused condition in `main.yaml`, which was removed.

Steps to reproduce: Insert a pending order while the app clock is ahead of the database clock, advance the app clock 5 minutes, run reconcile.
What was wrong and the fix applied: Orders and listings took `created_at` from the database clock (`now()`), while 'older than 10 minutes' and 'older than 60 days' were measured with the app clock. Rules that compare the two only work when both clocks agree. The repositories now store the creation time the service set from the app clock (`OrderRepo.insertPending`, `ListingRepo.insert`).
The organization denies every region except us-east-1, us-west-2 and ap-southeast-2. Defaults in `deploy.sh`, `teardown.sh`, `oidc.sh` and the deploy workflow are now ap-southeast-2.

Steps to reproduce: Create the stack: the Cdn resource fails.
What was wrong and the fix applied: CloudFront returns Your account must be verified before you can add new CloudFront resources". Needs AWS Support. The demo does not use CloudFront."

Steps to reproduce: Let the stack fail while RDS is creating.
What was wrong and the fix applied: Rollback ended in ROLLBACK_FAILED because the delete-time snapshot is refused while the instance is not available. Waited for available, then deleted the stack.

Steps to reproduce: Run deploy.sh without access to a Docker daemon.
What was wrong and the fix applied: The script built an image even with zero tasks. `INFRA_ONLY=1` exits after the stack is created.

Bundle ids differ per region (small_3_0 vs small_3_2), the account cannot create a small plan, a key pair cannot share the instance name, and rsync is not installed. Script uses micro_3_2, navya-demo-key and tar over ssh.

Steps to reproduce: Run `infra/lightsail-demo.sh db` with the generated master password.
What was wrong and the fix applied: The password has shell characters. Sourcing .env on the VM failed so the data copy did not run, and fragments of the password appeared in the output. The script now sets its own hex password and reads .env with grep. The password was replaced on the second run.
